stem:
Hema needs the additive inverse of $0$. The two integers in an inverse pair have equal distance from zero.

One or more options may be correct. Which two claims are correct?

options.text: $0+0=0$, so $0$ cancels with itself to zero.
Any integer can be the additive inverse of $0$, even one that is not at equal distance from zero.

teacher.key_rationale: Zero is its own additive inverse because 0+0=0. Calling +1 the opposite swaps the inverse. Allowing any integer omits equal distance from zero.
